title: Micro-goal anchor — weekly check-in & retro
content:
Purpose / tone
- Quick, messy weekly log for holding small commitments accountable. Not an org doc. Mostly for tracking signal: what moved, what stalled, what hypothesis to run next.

One-line weekly commitment
- Ship 2 developer-facing examples (python + ts) for the streaming SDK and carve out 3 focused deep blocks (90m each) Monday/Wednesday/Friday morning.

Quarterly objective (current)
Objective: Make onboarding for the SDK friction-free so a new engineer can call the hosted API and run a streaming example within 30 minutes.
Key results (my slice):
  KR1: 80% of example README steps verified by automated smoke tests (target: 4 smoke tests) — current: 2/4 (50%)
  KR2: 3 cross-language examples with CI (python, ts, go) — current: python + ts done, go blocked by packaging (66%)
  KR3: Reduce issue-first response time on SDK repo from median 28h -> <12h — current: 26h

This week's snapshot (metrics & energy)
- Deep work blocks completed: 2/3 (missed Wed block due to support rotation)
- PRs opened: 3 (examples: python streaming, ts streaming, docs fixes)
- PRs merged: 1 (python streaming)
- CI flakes encountered: 2 (integration container timing)
- Support threads responded within 6h: 4/6
- Focus hours (booked, not all productive): 14/20
- Energy: high mornings Mon/Tue, low Thurs (ran out of context-switch budget)

Wins
- Python streaming example merged and smoke test added (small victory)
- Found a flaky step in the integration matrix and isolated to container startup race
- Good async thread with Maya about onboarding checklist; got alignment on required bits for README

Misses / blockers
- TS example stalled on a bundling issue with the bundler config (esbuild flags) — needs someone from infra-ish to confirm runtime shim
- Go example deprioritized but still on my plate; need to scope a minimal example (no full SDK wrappers)
- Support rotation knocked out my Wednesday deep block — need to protect blocks better or schedule rotation differently

Hypotheses to test (micro-experiments)
1) Timeboxing first 90 minutes with Slack muted + "do-not-disturb" yields 2x throughput on code tasks. Experiment: run this for 5 consecutive working days and measure PR progress (baseline: 0.6 PR/day).
2) Moving the heavy CI matrix to nightly reduces flakes during daytime runs by >50% because cloud warm-start variability is lower at night. Run an A/B: daytime vs nightly re-runs for next 2 weeks.
3) Minimal Go example (one-file HTTP streaming example) will unblock >75% of installation questions — if true, then prioritize.

Tactical plan for next 7 days
- Monday: finish TS bundler tweak (pair with DevOps 30m), unblock CI flags (blocker: esbuild).
- Tuesday: add nightly CI schedule; open ticket to move long-running matrix off PR gate (JIRA DEVEX-2123).
- Wednesday: deep block (protected) — scope go minimal example; write quick README template.
- Thursday: triage support threads and merge any remaining tiny fixes.
- Friday: polish README and run a 30-minute playtest with a new hire (Maya volunteered).

Action items (concrete)
- [ ] Pair with Alex (infra) on esbuild flags (Slack thread: #devex, ping Alex)
- [ ] Add two more smoke tests to reach 4/4 (tests: stream connect, interrupt, token refresh, backpressure)
- [ ] Create minimal go example repo skeleton and link in README
- [ ] Move long-nightly CI step: open PR changing schedulers and document reasoning

Open questions / notes to self
- Is the onboarding target (30 minutes) realistic if we include KMS/HSM notes for private deployments? Might need a 'quickstart-lite' and 'enterprise-quickstart'.
- Consider adding a tiny checklist in each example: "What to try if it fails" — reduces first-time-ask support volume.
- If timeboxing experiment fails, try energy-based scheduling: critical tasks in 50–90m windows but on days with high energy only.

Signals to watch next week
- KR progress: smoke tests bumped to 3/4; go example scaffolded; median response time to new issues improves to <20h.
- CI flake count drops by at least 30% after nightly move.
- Deep-block completion ratio improves to 3/3.

Retro notes (quick)
- Keep: small daily wins narrative in PR descriptions — it helps momentum and reviewers.
- Stop: allowing support rotation to land in the middle of protected blocks; communicate availability windows earlier.
- Start: demoing examples to one new person each Friday to validate clarity.

Random friction log (quick capture)
- local docker network slow on Mac M2 — try Linux runner as comparison
- windows path issues in go example (file path separators) — add CI smoke on windows if we expand go example

Timestamp / context
- Logged: 2026-02-20 (end-of-week capture).
- Context: personal working notes for engineering-developer-experience tasks; may be copied to a more formal Confluence page if examples are published.
